page.layout: Two coin medallions at the top of the page (illustrations, no text block). Below them one column of running text, with italic verse set in the middle of the text. No margin notes, no notes under the text.

ceps, externorum primus, Romae imperat anno mundi 4060.

main_text.l: Hic Armeniam, Assyriam, Mesopotamiam, postea Arabiam
provincias fecit. in mari rubro classem instituit, ut per eam In-
diæ fines vastaret. Gloriam tamen militarem civilitate & mo-
deratione superavit: liberalis in omnes fuit: immunitates civi-
tatibus tribuit. amicis culpantibus quòd nimis circa
omnes comis esset, respondit, Talem se Imperatorem esse priuatis, quales esse
sibi Imperatores priuatus optasset[?]. in summa, Deo proximus habitus
est. E Perfide rediens profluvio vetris obiit anno ætatis 62. im-
perij ferè 20. Eutr. lib. 8. Aure. Vict. fuit paululum cibo, vinoque
deditus.
PLOTINA Traiani vxor fuit, quæ tam modestè & sanctè
in summa se potestate gesit, ut de ea nullus iure conqueri
potuerit. huius factione Tatianus Traiani Procurator, Adrianū
Imperatorem declaravit, cum sine liberis excesfisset Traia-
nus, & hæc Adriani amore flagraret, qui vicinus & potens erat.
Dion Cassius.

page.notes: The two medallions are engraved coins with legends in the image. Left medallion: a laureate bust with legend "TRAIANVS" and, at the upper right, "HADRI·IMP·AVG", both only partly legible at the edge of the engraving. Right medallion: a draped female bust with legend "PLOTINA AVG" and "TRAIANI VXOR". These are engraved within the illustrations and are not transcribed as running text. "Perfide" is printed as such (possibly for "Persida"); left as printed. "optasset" is doubtful in the print, marked [?]. "2o." after "ferè" is read as 20.
